page.title: Build Apps — Pranav PT
page.description: How do apps actually work internally? Understand frontend, backend, databases, and APIs — explained simply so you can eventually build your own.

sections.headline: Every app is just layers talking to each other.
sections.subheadline: Once you understand the three layers — frontend, backend, and database — every app in the world makes sense.

sections.title: The Three Layers of Every App
sections.subtitle: Think of it like a restaurant.

layers.name: Frontend
layers.analogy: The dining room — what the customer sees and touches.
layers.description: Everything you see on screen: buttons, layouts, text, forms. Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript.

layers.name: Backend
layers.analogy: The kitchen — where the real work happens.
layers.description: Processes your requests, applies business logic, communicates with the database. Built with Node, Python, etc.

layers.name: Database
layers.analogy: The pantry — where everything is stored.
layers.description: Stores all user data, content, records. Accessed only by the backend, never directly by the frontend.

sections.title: What is an API?
sections.body: An API is a waiter. The frontend (dining room) tells the waiter what it needs. The waiter goes to the kitchen (backend), gets what's required, and brings it back. The frontend never talks directly to the kitchen. That's the API — a defined contract for how layers communicate.

visual.description: Restaurant analogy: customer → waiter (API) → kitchen → waiter → customer

cards.title: API
cards.description: The contract that lets different parts of a system communicate.

cards.title: Authentication

cards.title: Deployment

cards.title: Version Control

cards.title: Frameworks
